About.title: About
About.whoBody: The Matmoora Memorial Center is a justice-oriented feminist organisation documenting systematic human rights violations and supporting community-led transitional and transformative justice in Sudan. Founded in 2021, Matmoora is a digital archive of political violence and an interactive platform for collective memory. Working from an intersectional, survivor-centered approach, we conduct investigative research and work in legal advocacy and grassroots capacity-building — preserving evidence, countering the erasure of narratives, and amplifying the voices of marginalised communities in pursuit of long-term accountability and community healing.
About.howBody: We follow a research methodology that begins with listening to the testimonies of survivors, then strengthening those testimonies through open-source investigation for accuracy and credibility. We then archive the testimonies and evidence, and — in partnership with individuals and grassroots groups — turn them into readable, listenable, and visual knowledge materials: research papers, stories, short films, and media campaigns.
About.visionBody: Justice for Sudanese people — the victims and survivors of political violence and human rights violations.
About.missionBody: We advocate for transitional justice in Sudan by exposing, documenting, preserving, and memorialising systemic, structural, and everyday violence across Sudan's regions and communities.
